name: Unboxing / first impressions
definition: A package arrives, gets opened on camera, and the product is revealed and tried for the first time. The anticipation (the box, the tape, the lid) is the hook and the genuine first reaction is the payoff; everything is filmed as it happens by the people receiving it.
why_it_sells: Among the dominant TikTok ecommerce formats. It hijacks the gift-opening reflex (viewers stay to see what is inside), the reveal frames the product as a treat worth waiting for, and the first reaction is social proof delivered in the moment. Group unboxings multiply that proof: several faces reacting at once reads as consensus.
visual_grammar: Four fixed moves in this order: the arrival (box carried toward the lens), the open (straight top-down on hands, tape and flaps), the reveal (a low POV from inside the box looking up at the faces, or a top-down lid lift), and the lift-out (the product raised to the lens, label first). Then first-use and reaction close-ups, one face per shot. The box and its inner packaging are part of the show: frost, liner, foam slots. The room is real and specific to the recipients.
camera: One phone handled by a friend in the room: handheld with quick reframes and the occasional whip pan to whoever speaks; top-down for the open; the inside-box POV is a phone set in the box; reaction close-ups at 50 to 80 cm. 24mm to 26mm phone lens, no gimbal, no dolly.
light: Whatever the room has, pushed by one strong source: here RGB gaming light (magenta and cyan) against warm overheads, with the cold white glow of the open box as the product's key light. Faces lit by screens.
texture: Phone video: sensor noise in the dark corners, mild sharpening, a touch of motion blur on fast hands, real skin, no grade beyond the RGB colour, no film grain.
palette_rule: Let the room's own lighting colours set the palette, keep the packaging neutral (kraft, silver liner, white foam) so the product is the one hero colour when it comes out of the box.
pacing: Arrival and a stakes line inside 2 s, the open by second 4, the reveal by second 7, the product name while it is held to the lens (at least 2.5 s), first-use and reactions cut fast at 1.8 to 2.4 s each, one real-life payoff that proves the reaction, then a direct-to-lens CTA from the person who opened it.
sound: The unboxing is an ASMR event: tape rip, cardboard flaps, a hiss of cold air, foam squeak, the can crack. Overlapping real voices, laughing, talking over each other. All native. Music only as a quiet hype bed in post, dropped for the tape rip and the brand line.

caption_look.active_word: #7FD3FF (cool sky blue) on the word being spoken
caption_look.position: centre, 64% down the frame, above the platform UI safe zone
caption_look.speaker_tag: tiny lower-case first name in 60% opacity above the caption box when the speaker changes

model_vocab: candid phone video frame, filmed by a friend in the room
straight top-down view of hands opening a box
low POV from inside the open box looking up at faces
RGB gaming room light, magenta and cyan
cold white glow from the open box
failure_modes: the shipping box comes back covered in fake courier labels and barcodes: say plain kraft cardboard with one plain sky-blue sticker and no text
the inside-box POV loses the box: say the camera sits on the foam inside the box, the four cardboard flaps frame the shot and the faces look down into it
the box is filled with the wrong cans or bottles: say the foam slots hold only cans exactly like the product reference, tops visible
group shots give two people one can, or someone holds two: say each person holds exactly one can
monitors and keyboards grow readable game UI and brand logos: say monitors show only abstract blurred colour, keyboards and headsets have no logos
the esports team jerseys pick up sponsor text: say plain sky-blue team jerseys with no text or logos
RGB light turns the can's sky-blue and silver to purple: say the can is lit by the white glow of the box or a neutral lamp so its colours stay true
cast looks like teenagers: state adult ages and say adults in their early twenties

reaction close-ups can come back as a giant disembodied head with the can floating on a table below: ask for head and chest with shoulders in natural proportion and the can in his own named hand, and push the coffee table out of frame
RGB living rooms fill with stray extra cans on the coffee table: say exactly one can in the whole frame for single-person shots
jersey colour drifts to black on close-ups: restate the plain sky-blue jersey in every shot prompt
prop sheets with 'two views' come back captioned with view names (closed, open): say unlabelled views and no captions on the sheet
a 'simple white bird silhouette' on a sky-blue banner renders as a real social network's logo: the team mark is an angular geometric falcon head, never a round songbird

a cluttered gamer room pulls in real merchandise: a sportswear swoosh on sneakers, a boxed vinyl figure, worded anime stickers on the fridge. Name every clutter item as unbranded and make stickers simple drawn shapes
a sky-blue jersey under an open hoodie turns into a basketball jersey with a team name across the chest: say plain jersey, no lettering or numbers, only the small falcon-head mark
'just lowered from his first sip' still renders the can at his lips: say held at chin height away from the lips, mouth clearly visible
negatives: no real brands, logos or signage except the product
no readable text generated by the model anywhere in the frame
no courier labels, barcodes or printed text on the box
no game interface or logos on screens
no more than one can per person
no round white songbird logo on blue
no sportswear logos or stripes on shoes, no boxed collectible figures, no character merchandise, no worded stickers
asset_style: Natural phone-photo realism, real skin texture, adults in their early twenties, not a studio headshot.
prompt_prefix: Candid smartphone video frame, vertical 9:16, filmed handheld by a friend in the room, 24mm phone lens, phone sensor noise, real available light, real skin, genuine unposed moment, not cinematic.
